examDifficulty.heading: What Does the Agentforce Revenue Management Consultant Exam Cover?
examDifficulty.summary: Salesforce describes this credential for consultants with broad Product-to-Cash knowledge and hands-on experience with Agentforce Revenue Management on core. The exam checks platform capability and implementation judgment, from catalog and pricing design through contracts, orders, assets, and invoicing.
bullets: 60 multiple-choice questions, plus up to five unscored questions in 105 minutes.
63% passing score, as listed in Salesforce’s current exam guide.
Seven exam objectives: platform concepts, implementation readiness, catalog management, Configure-Price-Quote, contracts and orders, asset management, and invoice management.
Design and delivery judgment: map customer requirements to platform capabilities, explain trade-offs, and plan implementation, testing, deployment, and adoption.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Use Salesforce’s current exam guide to structure study by objective. Practise mapping business requirements to out-of-the-box capabilities, then explain the licenses, configuration, trade-offs, test plan, and adoption steps the solution needs.

examFormat.heading: Agentforce Revenue Management Consultant Exam Format
examFormat.intro: Salesforce lists 60 multiple-choice questions, up to five unscored questions, and 105 minutes. The current guide organizes tested knowledge into seven objective areas:
bestWayToPass: Plan for implementation readiness: Review licenses, permission sets, feature prerequisites, stakeholder responsibilities, project scope, risk, testing, deployment, and adoption.
Design product catalogs: Know how catalog categories, product classifications, attributes, products, and bundles support customer requirements.
Configure products and pricing: Practise product configuration and validation, pricing procedures, and generating accurate quotes for a stated business case.
Connect the post-quote lifecycle: Study current Salesforce Contracts, Order Management, Asset Management, and Invoice Management capabilities and their role in Product-to-Cash delivery.

certificationCard.description: The Salesforce Certified Agentforce Revenue Management Consultant exam validates the ability to scope, design, build, and deploy the Agentforce Revenue Management product on core across the Product-to-Cash lifecycle.

keyConcepts.h2: Agentforce Revenue Management Consultant: Key Exam Concepts

blocks.heading: Platform Concepts and Implementation Readiness
blocks.body: The current exam guide covers Agentforce Revenue Management capabilities, its core data model, constraints, and trade-offs. Implementation readiness includes checking required licenses, permission sets, and feature prerequisites; assigning stakeholder responsibilities; creating scope and project plans; identifying risks; and planning build, test, deployment, and adoption. It also expects basic awareness of Flow, Lightning page components, Context Service, OmniStudio, Business Rules Engine, and APIs.

blocks.heading: Catalog Management and Product Configuration
blocks.body: Catalog Management organizes product information as a reusable source for selling. Salesforce preparation material covers product categories, classifications, attributes, products, and bundles. In the product-configuration objective, use the Product Configurator to customize product components and attributes, validate a configuration, and select out-of-the-box functionality that meets the stated requirement. See Salesforce’s [Product Catalog Management module](https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/product-catalog-management-with-revenue-cloud) for product and bundle coverage.

blocks.heading: Pricing and Quote Design
blocks.body: The Configure, Price, Quote objective asks candidates to use the Product Configurator and configure pricing procedures for customer-specific business cases. A consultant should translate requirements into an accurate quote, explain the selected pricing solution, and identify when an API or customization is needed. Salesforce’s current preparation trail includes Salesforce Pricing, Price Management, Advanced Price Management, and Transaction Management.

blocks.heading: Contracts, Orders, and Asset Lifecycle
blocks.body: The exam guide treats Salesforce Contracts and Order Management as separate objectives and also tests Asset Management. Salesforce preparation material includes digital contract management, order orchestration, and managing assets across the customer relationship. In a solution scenario, identify the out-of-the-box contract, order, or asset capability that fits the required process, then account for its implementation and lifecycle implications.

blocks.heading: Invoice and Usage Management
blocks.body: Invoice Management is an explicit current exam objective. The official preparation trail covers billing basics, automating invoices, managing payments and credits, and tracking billing data. It also introduces Usage Management for modeling and tracking usage-based products and preparing usage data for invoicing. Match the capability to the business’s billing and usage requirement rather than assuming a particular legacy object flow.

scenarioTips.h2: How to Prepare for the Agentforce Revenue Management Consultant Exam
scenarioTips.intro: Use the current Salesforce exam objectives to organize preparation around platform concepts, implementation readiness, catalog management, product configuration and pricing, contracts and orders, assets, and invoicing.

blocks.heading: Start with implementation readiness
blocks.body: For a customer scenario, identify the licenses, permission sets, prerequisites, stakeholders, scope, risks, and adoption work needed before deciding how to configure the solution.

blocks.heading: Translate catalog needs into product setup
blocks.body: Map catalog requirements to product categories, classifications, attributes, products, and bundles. For configuration questions, explain how the Product Configurator customizes and validates product components.

blocks.heading: Choose pricing and quote capabilities
blocks.body: Given customer-specific requirements, decide how to configure pricing procedures and generate an accurate quote. Be ready to state solution trade-offs and when to involve a developer for an API or customization.

blocks.heading: Trace the post-quote process
blocks.body: Recognize where Salesforce Contracts, Order Management, Asset Management, and Invoice Management fit the customer’s Product-to-Cash requirements. Account for order fulfillment, post-sale asset lifecycle, invoicing, payments, and credits where relevant.

blocks.heading: Plan delivery and prove the design
blocks.body: A complete solution includes stakeholder alignment, a project plan, risk mitigation, testing, deployment, and adoption. Practise explaining why the chosen out-of-the-box capability fits the business requirement and what constraints remain.

sampleQuestions.question: Which sequence best describes the Product-to-Cash lifecycle covered by Agentforce Revenue Management?
options: Product catalog and configuration, pricing and quote, then contracts, orders, assets, and invoicing
sampleQuestions.explanation: Salesforce describes the credential as spanning Product-to-Cash and its guide includes catalog, Configure-Price-Quote, contracts and orders, asset management, and invoice management.
whyWrong: Marketing alone does not cover the Product-to-Cash objectives.
The exam includes capabilities beyond the sales pipeline.
Service case management is not the lifecycle described in the current exam objectives.

sampleQuestions.question: What does the current Agentforce Revenue Management Consultant credential validate?
options: Visual design of CRM pages only
Scoping, designing, building, and deploying Agentforce Revenue Management solutions on core across Product-to-Cash
sampleQuestions.explanation: Salesforce’s current exam guide describes the credential as validating the ability to scope, design, build, and deploy the on-core product across Product-to-Cash.
whyWrong: Email marketing is a separate credential area.
Slack administration is a separate product specialty.
Page configuration is one platform capability, not the full consultant role.

sampleQuestions.question: Which set best matches the current Agentforce Revenue Management exam scope?
options: Catalog management, product configuration and pricing, contracts and orders, asset management, and invoice management
Only legacy Salesforce CPQ product rules
sampleQuestions.explanation: Salesforce’s current exam guide lists catalog management, Configure-Price-Quote, contracts and orders, asset management, and invoice management as exam objectives.
whyWrong: The current exam is broader than legacy CPQ product rules.
Marketing Cloud journeys are outside these listed objectives.
Opportunities alone do not cover the Product-to-Cash capabilities tested.

sampleQuestions.question: Which capability in Agentforce Revenue Management supports modeling and tracking usage-based products for invoicing?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Salesforce’s preparation trail describes Usage Management as modeling, tracking, and managing usage-based products through invoice-ready summaries.
whyWrong: Sales Cloud forecasting does not model usage measures for invoicing.
Automation Studio is a Marketing Cloud tool.
Chatter is a collaboration feature, not a usage billing capability.

sampleQuestions.question: Which capability organizes products and bundles using catalog categories and classifications?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Salesforce’s Product Catalog Management learning module covers organizing catalogs, products, and bundles with categories and classifications.
whyWrong: Invoice payment processing happens later in the revenue lifecycle.
Setup Audit Trail records administrative changes and does not manage products.
Email Studio is part of Marketing Cloud and does not manage the Revenue Management catalog.

sampleQuestions.question: In Agentforce Revenue Management, what does the Product Configurator help a consultant do?
options: Set permission set assignments for users
Customize product components and attributes, then validate the configuration
sampleQuestions.explanation: Salesforce’s current exam guide includes using the Product Configurator to customize product components and attributes and validate a product configuration.
whyWrong: Email sends are outside product configuration.
Permission sets are part of platform readiness, not product configuration.
Dashboards are not the Product Configurator’s purpose.

sampleQuestions.question: Which capability should a consultant consider for managing digital customer agreements in the Product-to-Cash process?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Salesforce’s preparation trail includes Salesforce Contracts Foundations and digital contract management as part of the revenue management implementation path.
whyWrong: Automation Studio is a Marketing Cloud tool.
Setup Audit Trail records administrative changes; it does not manage customer agreements.
Chatter is a collaboration feature, not contract management.

sampleQuestions.question: Which statement best describes Usage Management in the current Revenue Management preparation material?
options: It models and tracks usage-based products and prepares usage summaries for invoicing
sampleQuestions.explanation: Salesforce’s preparation trail describes Usage Management as modeling, tracking, and managing usage-based products through invoice-ready summaries.
whyWrong: Email journeys are unrelated to Revenue Management usage tracking.
User roles are part of implementation and access configuration.
Usage Management complements rather than replaces catalog management.

sampleQuestions.question: A customer needs orders fulfilled through defined orchestration processes after a sale. Which objective area is most relevant?
sampleQuestions.explanation: The current exam guide includes Contracts and Orders, and the preparation trail covers order management and order orchestration for order fulfillment.
whyWrong: Email marketing is a separate product domain.
Subscriber data is a Marketing Cloud concern.
Knowledge articles are unrelated to order orchestration.

sampleQuestions.question: What is a key part of implementation readiness for an Agentforce Revenue Management project?
options: Choosing a CPQ price book before gathering requirements
Confirming licenses, permission sets, prerequisites, scope, stakeholders, and adoption plan
Assuming every customer uses the same product configuration
Skipping build and testing to shorten delivery
sampleQuestions.explanation: The current exam guide includes required licenses, permission sets, prerequisite feature toggles, stakeholder roles, scope and project planning, risk mitigation, testing, deployment, and adoption.
whyWrong: The guide emphasizes readiness and customer requirements rather than assuming an implementation detail.
Solutions should translate customer requirements into appropriate capabilities.
The exam guide explicitly includes build, test, deployment, and adoption.

sampleQuestions.question: Which capability area is used to track products and services a customer has purchased after the sale?
sampleQuestions.explanation: Salesforce’s preparation trail includes Asset Lifecycle Management and describes managing assets to support post-sale customer relationships.
whyWrong: A catalog organizes products for selling; it does not represent the customer’s purchased asset lifecycle.
Business Rules Engine supports decision automation but is not the asset lifecycle capability.
Email Studio is a Marketing Cloud application.

sampleQuestions.question: A customer needs accurate quotes for different business cases. Which approach is covered by the current Configure, Price, Quote objective?
options: Configure pricing procedures for the customer requirements and generate an accurate quote
Replace catalog attributes with free-text notes
Defer pricing decisions until after order fulfillment
sampleQuestions.explanation: The current exam guide asks candidates to configure pricing procedures for customer-specific business cases and generate accurate pricing quotes.
whyWrong: Invoice management is a later, separate objective.
The Product Configurator and catalog use structured product information.
Pricing and quote generation occur before downstream orders and fulfillment.

sampleQuestions.question: When should a consultant identify a need for an API or customization?
options: For every catalog item, regardless of requirements
Whenever a user needs a permission set
When customer requirements cannot be met by the appropriate out-of-the-box capability and an extension is needed
sampleQuestions.explanation: The current exam guide expects candidates to identify when APIs or customizations are needed and describe the requirements to a developer.
whyWrong: The guide emphasizes choosing capabilities based on the customer case, not custom development by default.
Permission sets are part of configuration and access readiness, not by themselves a reason for an API.
The guide expects consultants to articulate solution trade-offs.

sampleQuestions.question: What is the purpose of organizing a product catalog with categories, classifications, and attributes?
options: To structure product information so products and bundles can be managed and configured for selling
To store marketing email engagement metrics
sampleQuestions.explanation: Salesforce’s Product Catalog Management material covers organizing product and bundle information with categories, classifications, and attributes.
whyWrong: Order Management is a separate downstream capability.
Payment and invoice functions are part of Invoice Management.
Email engagement metrics belong to Marketing Cloud.

sampleQuestions.question: Which delivery practice is explicitly included in Salesforce’s current Revenue Management consultant exam guide?
options: Skip user acceptance testing after configuration
Plan and lead discovery, mitigate risks, test, deploy, and drive adoption
Focus only on writing custom code
Avoid stakeholder alignment once a quote is generated
sampleQuestions.explanation: The current guide includes discovery and design, project planning, risk mitigation, stakeholder alignment, build, testing, deployment, and adoption.
whyWrong: The preparation trail includes user acceptance testing, and the guide covers testing.
The guide expects basic API and customization awareness, not a code-only focus.
Stakeholder alignment and business value are explicitly part of the consultant role.
